publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: These anyons can be used to perform universal quantum computation.

span.label: anyonic excitations in two-dimensional lattice spin models
span.quote: Excitations in this model are anyons, meaning that the global wavefunction acquires some phase factor when one excitation moves around the other.

span.label: theoretical-construction
span.quote: From now on, we are constructing and studying nonabelian anyons which will allow universal quantum computation.

span.label: real quantum systems suffer decoherence and systematic errors
span.quote: decoherence and systematic errors in unitary transformations which occur in real quantum systems

span.label: For the abelian toric-code memory the author has no way to read information into or out of the protected space.
span.quote: Unfortunately, I do not know any way this quantum information can get in or out.

span.label: The gate set obtainable by braiding abelian anyons is not universal.
span.quote: Too few things can be done by moving abelian anyons.

span.label: The group used for the universal-computation construction is physically implausible.
span.quote: (The group S5 is quite unrealistic for physical implementation).

span.label: No general theory underlies the constructions given.
span.quote: A general theory of anyons and topological quantum order is lacking.

span.label: The universal-computation results are stated without full derivation, to appear elsewhere.
span.quote: (This section should be considered as an abstract of results to be presented elsewhere).

span.label: The number the whole fault-tolerance argument depends on is declared unknown in a footnote, with estimates three orders of magnitude apart.
span.quote: Actually, the threshold is not known. Estimates vary from 1/300 [7] to 10−6 [4]

span.label: The case that errors can be corrected by physics rather than by procedure is made by analogy with magnetic storage, and hedged.
span.quote: This process is quite similar to the standard error correction procedure for the repetition code. We may say that errors are being corrected at the physical level

span.label: The protection is degeneracy of a ground state on a surface, so the quantity protected depends on the topology chosen.
span.quote: The ground state of this Hamiltonian coincides with the protected space of the code. It is 4g-fold degenerate, where g is the genus of the surface

span.label: fault tolerance - BY PHYSICS RATHER THAN BY PROCEDURE: Shor's construction simulates a circuit with imperfect gates given a precision threshold, whereas here the computation is said to be fault-tolerant by its physical nature, so the two uses of the phrase name a software guarantee and a property of a material
span.quote: Such computation is fault-tolerant by its physical nature

span.label: the threshold - A NUMBER THE ARGUMENT NEEDS AND NOBODY HAS: the text calls it rather small and very difficult to achieve, and the footnote says outright that it is not known, giving estimates that differ by orders of magnitude
span.quote: Unfortunately, the threshold value of δ is rather small1; it is very difficult to achieve this precision

span.label: the protected space - AS A DEGENERATE GROUND STATE: it coincides with the ground state of a Hamiltonian built from local stabilizer operators, and its size is set by the genus of the surface rather than by anything about the computation
span.quote: The ground state of this Hamiltonian coincides with the protected space of the code. It is 4g-fold degenerate, where g is the genus of the surface

span.label: builds-on → quantum error-correcting codes (stabilizer codes)
span.quote: we need a quantum code with local stabilizer operators

span.label: builds-on → stabilizer quantum codes on lattices on the torus and other 2-D surfaces [6, 8]
span.quote: I start with a class of stabilizer quantum codes associated with lattices on the torus and other 2-D surfaces [6, 8].

span.label: extends → G. Castagnoli and M. Rasetti's use of one-dimensional anyons for quantum computation [14]
span.quote: An attempt to use one-dimensional anyons for quantum computation was made by G. Castagnoli and M. Rasetti [14], but the question of fault-tolerance was not considered.

span.label: builds-on → Einarsson's proof that ground state degeneracy on the torus follows from the existence of anyons [19]
span.quote: Here is the original Einarsson’s proof applied to our two types of particles.

span.label: protected space —same-as→ ground state
span.quote: The ground state of this Hamiltonian coincides with the protected space of the code

span.label: anyonic excitations —causes→ fault-tolerant
span.quote: A two-dimensional quantum system with anyonic excitations can be considered as a quantum computer. Unitary transformations can be performed by moving the excitations around each other. Measurements can be performed by joining excitations in pairs and observing the result of fusion. Such computation is fault-tolerant by its physical nature

span.label: 4g-fold — ground-state degeneracy of the toric-code Hamiltonian, g = genus of the surface
span.quote: It is 4g-fold degenerate, where g is the genus of the surface.

span.label: ΔE = 2 — energy gap separating excited states (eigenvalue difference of the stabilizer operators)
span.quote: All excited states are separated by an energy gap ∆E 2, because the difference between the eigenvalues of As or Bp equals 2.

span.label: A 2D quantum system with anyonic excitations can act as a quantum computer: unitary gates are performed by braiding excitations around each other, measurement by fusing them.
span.quote: A two-dimensional quantum system with anyonic excitations can be considered as a quantum computer. Unitary transformations can be performed by moving the excitations around each other.

span.label: Fault tolerance is intrinsic and topological: the ground-state degeneracy is protected against local perturbations, so errors are corrected at the physical level.
span.quote: The degeneracy is persistent to local perturbation.

span.label: braiding of anyonic excitations
span.quote: Such motion (“braiding”) can be considered as fault-tolerant quantum computation.

span.label: degenerate ground state (encoded qubit)
span.quote: the degenerate state undergoes a nontrivial unitary transformation when one particle moves around the other

span.label: nonabelian anyons
span.quote: These particles are nonabelian anyons, i.e. the degenerate state undergoes a nontrivial unitary transformation when one particle moves around the other.

span.label: braiding
span.quote: moving the excitations around each other

span.label: mean
span.quote: If the gauge symmetry is broken then there is a nonvanishing vacuum average of the Higgs field, φ(s) = = 0.

span.label: null-hypothesis
span.quote: In particular, 0 = U H0 U † = H ′ 0 ≡ − X s σx s − X p σz p (8) 1, Qp ≡ H ′ In the field theory language, the vertex variables vs (or the operators σz s ) are a Higgs field.

span.label: standard-error
span.quote: This process is quite similar to the standard error correction procedure for the repetition code.
